problem: The sentence says a rollup 'posts compressed data plus a proof back' and then describes optimistic rollups. An optimistic rollup does not post any proof when it posts data; it posts data plus a bond and relies on a challenge window, with a fraud proof produced only if someone challenges. A student can read the sentence as saying every rollup posts a proof.
fix: A rollup runs transactions off-chain and posts compressed data back to layer 1 with a bond; it may also post a proof. A ZK rollup posts a validity proof with every batch, so each batch is final once verified. An optimistic rollup posts only the data and a bond, assumes correctness, and lets anyone submit a fraud proof during the challenge window.

problem: 'Only endorsed parties can read through chaincode' is loose. The private payload goes to the peers of the organisations named in the collection policy, which is not the same set as the endorsing peers of one transaction.
fix: A private data collection puts a hash on the shared channel ledger and keeps the payload in a private side database on the peers of the organisations named in the collection policy; those peers read it through chaincode, while other channel members see only the hash.
